answer.part: Battle procedure from ambush through removal
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing containing your warriors or pawn and an enemy defender; rule is not required. Defender may play a matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals no hits; otherwise defender immediately deals two hits and discards it. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Resolve before-roll effects (attacker orders if both sides have effects), roll (higher die is attacker's hits, lower defender's; equal dice equal hits), then resolve after-roll effects (attacker orders if both sides have effects). Rolled hits are capped by each side's own warriors, except Alliance defenders reverse dice and Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead. Count extra hits (uncapped), subtract ignored hits, and add one defenseless hit if defender has no warriors (Vagabond instead has no undamaged swords). On dealing hits, each side chooses its own removal order, but warriors must be removed before its buildings/tokens; each side orders effects from its own pieces' removal. Both sides deal counted hits even if warriors were removed after rolling. Whoever removes enemy buildings/tokens scores one VP each, including defenders and removals outside battle.

answer.ruling: In your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP.

At the start of your own Birdsong, win by ruling three clearings of the matching mouse, rabbit or fox suit, or for bird dominance by ruling two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately.
You cannot remove or replace an activated dominance card.
Whenever a dominance card would enter the discard pile, put it near the map as available instead.

During your Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into your hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so the payment must be a bird card; a bird card can pay for a non-bird dominance card.
With two players remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and deal three cards to each player.

Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The map supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea and 2 coins. Only if Vagabond is in play, its four R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword are each hidden under one ruin after shuffling the ruin/item stacks; without Vagabond ruins have no hidden items.
Set up factions in order Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond; this is distinct from turn order.
Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. If removed, the Keep cannot be placed again.

Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply. This can happen outside battle; without a Keep there is no hospital destination.
The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.
First craft with workshops, then take up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number subject to Recruit's limit.
One March action permits up to two moves; either may use the same or different warriors. The compound action cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action.
Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and can be taken only once per turn; if supply cannot fill all, place the maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.
Spend a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.

Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and a building type; take the leftmost building of that type from its track. Pay the cost atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or other ruled clearings linked to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score VP on the newly uncovered space. Full wood cost, the building piece, and a legal slot are required.
In order: Emergency Orders (if hand empty, draw one); add one or two hand cards to any Decree columns, with at most one bird card; then New Roost if no roosts are on the map.
Place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.

Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card by columns Recruit, Move, Battle, Build. A Recruit card matches a clearing with a roost and places one warrior at one chosen roost (two for Charismatic); Move matches the origin and moves at least one warrior under normal movement rules; Battle matches the battle clearing and initiates a battle with Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build matches the target clearing and places one roost there.
Within each column, choose card order freely. Bird cards are wild in every column, while action requirements still apply.

Build must place a roost in a clearing you rule with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required Decree action cannot be fully completed, immediately enter Turmoil; do not skip that card or continue to other columns.

Lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none are face up, turn all leaders face up first); retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings.
Turmoil ends Daylight, then the normal Evening still occurs: score the roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, and discard to five.
answer.evidence: Eyrie: Turmoil; Evening, even after turmoil.

answer.ruling: When another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters per affected move, not per warrior. If there is no matching card including birds, show your hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters.
If Supporters is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; the payment or no-match draw still occurs.

Both Revolt and Spread Sympathy occur in Birdsong; complete all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy. Each may be performed any number of times, and once spreading starts you cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong.

Choose a sympathetic clearing without a base that matches a base still on your board; spend two matching supporters (birds wild). Remove all enemy pieces there, score one VP per enemy building/token removed, place the matching base, place warriors equal to sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit (including this clearing), and place one warrior in Officers. Resolve even if placement is short; place the maximum possible. Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.

answer.part: Spread Sympathy eligibility, cost and result
answer.ruling: Choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if no sympathy is on the map. Spend supporters matching the target suit as shown above the next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter if the target has at least three warriors of one other player (Martial Law). Place the token and score the uncovered space. Only one sympathy per clearing; Keep's placement ban applies.

During Daylight, Train by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. During Evening, Organize is one military operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, and score uncovered VP; it has no supporter, adjacency or Martial Law cost, but legal token placement is required.
When a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing, including birds, and remove half your officers rounded up. If no bases remain, discard excess Supporters down to five.

answer.ruling: Birdsong Refresh: count tea already face up on Refresh track, flip two exhausted items face up per tea, then three more; tea refreshed during the step gives no extra refresh then. Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out of a clearing. Forest adjacency is defined by touching clearings without crossing a printed path or forests separated by one printed path; Winter's river also divides forests.

During Daylight, exhaust one boot plus one extra boot if destination contains any warriors of any Hostile faction (also for forced moves). Ignore rule. Cannot enter a forest with this action; from a forest, move only to an adjacent clearing.

In Evening, if in a forest return all damaged items to Satchel and flip them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able. Always draw one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest; then discard to five and perform the final capacity check.
Exhaust torch in a ruin's clearing; take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track, scoring one VP if an item is taken. Remove the ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.

In a matching clearing choose a face-up matching quest; exhaust its two listed items, complete it, then choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards. Draw a replacement quest into the display; no card is spent.
Exhaust a hammer and move one damaged item to Satchel, keeping its current face; ready tea, coins or bags move to tracks if space permits.
Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except for the special allied-warrior battle-loss rule.

During battle on Vagabond's own turn, score one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile. A hostile building/token is normally two VP total (one removal VP plus one Infamy); the first hostile warrior gives no Infamy. Infamy is turn-based and does not apply on another player's turn or to Strike.

Aid cannot move a marker out of Hostile, though Vagabond may still take a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it remove another piece of that faction. Strike does not score Infamy.
With four or more players, during Vagabond's Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate dominance to form a coalition.

Choose a player not already in a coalition whose VP is lowest among all players other than Vagabond (choose among ties). Put Vagabond's score marker on that faction board and stop scoring; if the partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including when the partner wins through dominance.
A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition partners are not enemies, and coalition does not grant Allied relationship powers.
Cards override Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. Follow general and faction rules together where possible, and faction rules prevail if incompatible.
“Cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden.
If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, the attacker chooses their order.
A Marquise March's two moves are one compound action; do not interrupt it to spend a bird card or take another action.
“At start” effects happen before all other effects in that phase; “at end” effects happen after everything else in that phase and before the next phase.

answer.part: Actions after last turn step begins
answer.ruling: Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening or end-of-turn actions.
Hand size is public but hand contents are private; reveal or show a hand only if explicitly instructed. Face-up piles can be searched or inspected; the deck cannot.
Agreements are non-binding; cards may be transferred only as instructed, and actions require no consent.
When the shared deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck.
Birds substitute for any non-bird suit; when instructed to give or discard cards of a non-bird suit, treat birds as that suit, with the instruction determining how many cards.
Only a bird card pays an explicit bird-card requirement; fox, rabbit and mouse cards cannot.
Pieces are finite and proxies are not allowed. If instructed to place more pieces than remain, do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily place fewer.

answer.ruling: Face-up tea, coins and bags in Satchel immediately move to empty matching track spaces if possible. Each type's track holds at most three. Exhausting a tracked item moves it to Satchel; if it is damaged it goes to the Damaged box without changing face.

Capacity is six items plus two per face-up bag on its track. Count items in Satchel plus Damaged box; items on tracks do not count.
Capacity is checked as the last step of Evening after drawing and discarding; it is not checked immediately upon gaining items. Permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within capacity.

Forest Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; ready tea, coins and bags move to tracks if able. It does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. You cannot use an ally's warriors to attack that ally itself.

answer.part: Hostility from allied warriors taking hits

Equal numbers do not trigger hostility. This special timing overrides ordinary hostility timing for these allied warriors removed against another enemy.
